newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks scramble to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks scramble to higher close.

text.p: Australian shares closed firmer on Monday after the market scrambled off its lows in the afternoon ahead of the September share index futures expiry.
The All Ordinaries index gained 7.4 points to 2290.40.
Grokers said a spurt of activity in the leaders in the afternoon saw the bourse head to higher ground.
"Turnover picked up towards the end and that kept the run going but there were no dramatic moves," said a Sydney dealer.
The Australian market has now finished higher for the fifth consecutive day.
Noting that mining stocks closed at their lows, the dealer said some shuffling had occurred in the afternoon and pointed to CRA, BHP and WMC as stocks to watch on Tuesday.
"BHP and WMC were tossed around a bit and there could be some moves there tomorrow after trade settles," he said.
BHP closed 15 cents lower at A$16.20 while WMC closed 17 cents lower at A$8.13.
Among industrial stocks, the big banks found favour as buyers went looking for yield.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about seven to five, while about 30 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
